concepts.name: One-Way ANOVA
concepts.description: A statistical hypothesis test used to compare the means of three or more independent groups based on a single categorical independent variable.

concepts.name: F-statistic
concepts.description: The test statistic computed in ANOVA as the ratio of mean square model variance to mean square error variance (MS_model / MS_error).

concepts.name: Partitioning Variance
concepts.description: The procedure of splitting total sum of squares (SStotal) into sum of squares explained by the model (SSmodel) and residual error sum of squares (SSerror).

concepts.name: Eta-squared (η²)
concepts.description: An effect size measure in ANOVA representing the proportion of total variance explained by group membership (SSmodel / SStotal).

concepts.name: Bonferroni Correction
concepts.description: A post-hoc adjustment method for multiple comparisons that multiplies p-values by the number of comparisons to control the familywise false-positive rate.

concepts.name: ANOVA Assumptions
concepts.description: Requirements for valid ANOVA inference including interval/ratio DV, independent observations, homogeneity of variance (tested via Levene's test), and normal distribution of residuals.

concepts.name: Between-Subjects Design
concepts.description: An experimental research design where separate, mutually exclusive groups of participants are exposed to different treatment conditions.

claims: t-tests are appropriate for comparing two groups, while ANOVAs are required when comparing more than two groups or conditions.
The total variance in a dependent variable is partitioned into variance explained by group membership (SSmodel) and residual variance (SSerror).
A statistically significant F-statistic indicates overall group differences exist, but post-hoc pairwise tests are needed to pinpoint which specific groups differ.
Performing multiple post-hoc t-tests increases the risk of Type I errors (false positives), requiring p-value adjustments like the Bonferroni correction.
ANOVA is robust to violations of normality and homogeneity of variance assumptions when sample sizes across groups are equal.
summary: This document presents lecture slides by Dr. Metodi Siromahov on One-Way Between-Subjects ANOVA. It explains the distinction between t-tests and ANOVA, demonstrates how total variance is partitioned into model and error sums of squares, and walks through calculating degrees of freedom, the F-statistic, and eta-squared effect size using a running speed dataset across three music tempo conditions. Additionally, it details executing ANOVA in R using the afex package, performing Bonferroni-corrected post-hoc pairwise comparisons, testing statistical assumptions, and structuring standard academic write-ups.
